cohort: The study included 61,605 first-time parturients who participated in the 2016 to 2019 Multistate Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS).
finding: After adjusting for maternal demographics and pregnancy characteristics, there was no significant association between antenatal depression and cesarean delivery among first-time parturients.
cross-section timing: Data from the 2016 to 2019 Multistate Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS) was used, with depression reported in the 3 months prior to or at any point during the recent pregnancy, and mode of delivery obtained from birth certificates.
